what_it_does: Tracing is a way of recording what a program does internally — which functions were called, in what order, with what timing — so engineers can diagnose performance problems. In a busy shared datacenter every fraction of a percent of extra CPU usage matters, but current tracing tools add 5–18% overhead to the applications being watched, making continuous tracing impractical. EXIST redesigns the entire trace recording pipeline to stay well under 1% overhead by using ultra-lightweight measurement hooks that do not stall the program, by recording and compressing trace events on a side path that never touches the program's critical work, and by discarding redundant events while preserving the causal chain needed to reconstruct what happened. This is from the abstract only; the exact overhead numbers should be verified from the full paper.
